skills.name: solo-workflow:review
helped: Structured the review (verdict, findings by severity, what holds up, what wasn't run) and named the planted-.npmrc route through the lab-up race.
skipped: Didn't dispatch Solo's reviewer or refuter agents although Agent was allowed; it said an independent review would be worthwhile instead.

checks.observed: Finding 3: while the lab is up, a running builder can plant an .npmrc in build/; --ignore-scripts still wins but registry= and other settings have no command-line override. Also lists, unconfirmed, that git dependencies' prepare scripts may run code despite --ignore-scripts.
evidence: with-review.md, finding 3 and 'Not covered or not run'

checks.observed: States that a builder-written package-lock.json's resolved URLs (and URL or git specs in package.json) make npm fetch from any host, including the reference's own package.

findings.summary: Review ran as a single self-review for a boundary change and didn't use Solo's reviewer agent, only recommended one.

limitations: One run per arm, so this is one sample each, not proof of cause.
Checks were written before the first attempt. For this attempt the scenario setup changed (version 2: Skill tool added, MCP connectors removed); the checks didn't.

First attempt (scenario version 1, not recorded as a run): the Skill tool was left out of both arms and 413 claude.ai connector tools were loaded, so the with arm could list Solo's skills but not load them. Both arms missed the npmrc check's strong form; about $4.75 per arm.
Both arms had one compound Bash read denied by the allowlist and said no checks or tests ran; the reviews come from reading code.

The npmrc check passes on the planted-.npmrc-changes-npm-behavior reading. Neither arm found the original blocker: a linked .npmrc that slips past the host-side existsSync check and makes the networked npm run code.
Subject fingerprint is the sha256 of the sorted per-file sha256 list of the installed Solo Workflow 0.4.0 plugin folder used with --plugin-dir.
